transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally scared me enough to come in is that I’ve been having these thoughts that maybe it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. Not that I’ve done anything to hurt myself — I haven’t — but the thought keeps coming around, and that’s not like how I want to be thinking, you know?

I kept telling myself maybe it would pass, or maybe I was just tired, but when you start lying there and thinking that not waking up sounds easier than facing another day… that frightened me. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, because I haven’t tried anything, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should tell someone instead of just keeping it in my head.
How long have you been feeling this way and having these thoughts?

It’s been… about four months, I’d say. I keep trying to mark it by when my aunt came to live with us, because that’s when I first really noticed I wasn’t just having a bad week or two. Since then it’s been hanging around, on and off, but there enough that I can’t pretend it’s nothing. So yes… around four months now.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with loved ones?

Yes… yes, I have. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel not like myself.

I used to really look forward to doing my watercolors. I’d set everything out, even if I wasn’t very good, and I’d lose track of time mixing colors or trying to paint flowers or little scenes. Now the paints just sit there. I see them, and I think, “I should do that,” but then I just… don’t. It feels like too much, or like there’s no point.

And I used to go to dance class, too. Nothing fancy, just something to get moving and be around people. I used to enjoy it more than I even admitted. But lately I can’t make myself go, and when I think about it, I don’t feel that little spark I used to.

Same with walking with the ladies. We’d go and talk, and it was nice, you know, having that routine. Now I find reasons not to, or I just don’t care enough to get myself ready. It’s not that I hate those things. It’s more like the feeling that made them matter has gone quiet.
Have you had days where you feel down or depressed most of the time, not just occasionally feeling sad or low?

Yes… most days, really. It’s not just like I get a little sad over something and then it passes. It’s more like I wake up already feeling weighed down.

Most mornings, before I’ve even done anything, there’s this heavy sadness sitting in my chest, like I’ve already failed the day before it even starts. I’ll just open my eyes and feel this sinking feeling, and I think, “Oh… here we go again.” It can make the whole day feel spoiled before I’ve even gotten out of bed.

Some parts of the day are quieter than others, I guess, but that low feeling is there a lot of the time. It’s like I’m carrying it around with me, even when nothing particular has happened right then.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed anything big that way. I mean… my eating is probably a little irregular some days, but I couldn’t honestly say I’ve been eating a lot more or a lot less in a way I’m sure about.

My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything, and I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you a number. Some days I don’t feel like bothering with food much, but then other days I’ll eat more normally, so it’s hard for me to tell if it really counts as a change. So… no, not really a clear appetite or weight change that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear change, not the way I could point to it and say, “Yes, this started happening.”

Some nights I might take a little while to settle, but I think I’ve always had nights like that here and there. And then other nights I sleep more or less normally, or at least I think I do. I haven’t been keeping track of the hours or anything. I’m not waking up thinking, “Oh, I barely slept,” every single day, but I also can’t say I’ve been sleeping wonderfully.

So… I guess no, not a big sleep change that I’ve really noticed. Nothing that stands out to me as much as some of the other things.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or perhaps feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yes… I think so. I didn’t notice it as much myself at first, but my husband has said a few times that I move like everything takes extra effort now. Like I’m not exactly unable to move, but I do things slower, like I have to push myself through each little step.

Even something simple, like going to the market… I’ll go in knowing what I came for, but then I’ll just stand there too long in front of the shelf before picking it up. It’s not that I’m comparing prices for a long time or anything smart like that. I’m just… standing there, like my body and my head are both delayed. Then I realize people are moving around me and I feel embarrassed.

I don’t know if I’d call it restlessness. It’s more the slow, stuck feeling. Like everything takes more effort than it should.
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much or that you're letting people down, even when there's no real reason for it?

Yes… I do get that feeling. It’s mostly around my aunt, honestly. If I feel tired, or if I get annoyed with her even a little, then afterward I start thinking, “What kind of woman am I?” Like I’m bad for even having that feeling.

I know people get tired, and I know nobody is cheerful and grateful every second, but in my head it turns into something bigger. I start thinking I’m bringing shame on my family, like I’m not being the kind of person I was supposed to be. Like I should be more grateful, more patient, more… I don’t know, decent.

And it can be over something small. She’ll need something, or say something, and I’ll feel irritated inside, and then I hate myself for it. I think, “A good woman wouldn’t feel that way.” So yes, I do feel like I’m letting people down, even when maybe there isn’t a clear reason.

Have there been any periods during these four months where your mood was low and you experienced several of these other symptoms — like loss of interest, feeling slowed down, or guilty — nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

Yes… I think so. It’s hard for me to separate it neatly into weeks, because I wasn’t marking it on a calendar or anything, but this whole thing has really been going on for about four months now, since my aunt came to live with us.

That’s when I started noticing I wasn’t feeling like myself most days. Not just one bad afternoon or a few days here and there, but it kind of settled over everything. So, yes, I’d say there have definitely been stretches longer than two weeks where I was low and feeling slowed down and guilty nearly every day. It’s been more or less part of these past four months.

Between these periods of feeling low and struggling with these symptoms, have you had any time where you felt back to your usual self — where your mood was stable, and you were able to enjoy things and function normally — for at least a couple of months?

No… not really. I wouldn’t say I’ve had a couple of months where I felt like myself again. This has been going on for about four months now, since my aunt came to live with us, and it’s felt pretty continuous to me.

I mean, there might be an hour here or there where I seem more normal, or I get through something without thinking about it so much, but that’s not the same as being back to myself. I can’t point to a long stretch where my mood was steady and I was functioning the way I used to. Since she moved in, it’s just kind of been… there, hanging over everything.
Before these past four months, have you ever had a period where you felt this low or struggled with similar symptoms for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure, doctor… I don’t think so, not like this. I’ve had hard times before, of course, and days where I felt sad or worn down, but I can’t really remember a stretch before these last four months where it stayed with me like this for two weeks or more.

I mean, I don’t want to say never if I’m forgetting something, because life has had its ups and downs, but nothing is standing out to me the way this does. This feels more… continuous, I guess. Before this, I think I would have bad days and then come back around more like myself.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable, where you felt more energetic or talkative than usual, or needed less sleep but still had lots of energy?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve had times where I was irritated, sure, like anybody does, especially when things are stressful, but not in the way you’re describing where I felt unusually high or full of energy.

I can’t remember any time where I suddenly needed less sleep and still felt energized, or where I was talking more than usual because I felt so good or revved up. That doesn’t really sound like me. If anything, when I’m not doing well, I tend to go the other direction.
Have you ever felt a complete loss of pleasure in all or almost all activities, or found that even things you usually enjoy don’t bring you any happiness at all?

Yes… yes, I think that’s been happening. I don’t know if I’d say every single thing in the whole world, but the things that used to feel like mine, the things I used to look forward to, they just don’t do anything for me lately.

I used to paint with my watercolors, and I’d fuss over the colors and the paper, and even if it wasn’t very good, it gave me a little peace. Now the paints are just sitting there. I see them and I think, “I should do that,” but I can’t make myself care enough to start.

Same with dance class. I used to enjoy going, even just seeing people and moving around a little. And walking with the ladies — that was something I looked forward to, just getting out and talking while we walked. But lately I don’t feel any happiness from it. I leave things sitting, I don’t go like I used to, and even when I think about it, there’s just this flat feeling, like it doesn’t matter.
